**Built `Servex/ext/openrouter/evals/probes.mjs`** per probes.md/probes.json's design, and ran it for real.

- [x] `--dry-run` prints model/probe/prompt/dir and spawns nothing — shown for page-blog and log-line.

- [x] `--selftest`: a deliberately broken page (unterminated backtick) scores 0 on checks 1 and 2, proving the checks can fail.

**What the control's own two runs found** (no a/b/c label yet — this IS the baseline): `page-blog` passed only check 1 (parses); `log-line` passed none of its one check. Haiku at low effort wrote good on-topic content both times but skipped the task system completely (no new-task, no task.jsonl under public/framework/ai/, nothing through append.mjs), and for page-blog it overwrote the scratch directory's own seeded page instead of adding a linked child page. Written up in the new Probe tasks section of `Servex/ext/openrouter/readme.md`.

**Left for task-mastermind-openrouter:** running the same two probes on real OpenRouter models is what turns this into an (a)/(b)/(c) verdict — right now there's only the one data point.

**A worktree was stale, fixed along the way:** this task's worktree (`worktree/proposal-flow`) was 34 commits behind `michael/dev` and missing the whole openrouter module and the probe-tasks design docs. Brought both in read-only (`git checkout michael/dev -- <path>`, then unstaged) rather than rebuilding them — logged as a decision above.

**Also found and fixed while proving `--selftest`:** plain `git status --porcelain` collapses a brand-new untracked directory into one line, so check 1 was silently "passing" without checking anything inside it; fixed with `-uall`.
